title: Enhanced Magnetocaloric Properties of the (MnNi)<sub>0.6</sub>Si<sub>0.62</sub>(FeCo)<sub>0.4</sub>Ge<sub>0.38</sub> High-Entropy Alloy Obtained by Co Substitution.

recollection.starting_material: A bulk high‐entropy alloy with nominal composition (MnNi)0.6Si0.62(FeCo)0.4Ge0.38, prepared by arc melting and subsequent homogenization.
recollection.intervention: Partial substitution of Co for Fe in the (MnNi)0.6Si0.62(FeCo)0.4Ge0.38 matrix, followed by annealing to promote phase uniformity (guess).
recollection.structure: A predominantly single‐phase hexagonal Ni2In−type structure with slight lattice parameter changes on Co substitution, plus minor secondary phases (guess).
recollection.mechanism: Tuning of the first‐order magnetostructural transition by Co‐induced modification of exchange interactions, which sharpens the magnetic entropy change near the Curie point (guess).
recollection.results: An enhanced isothermal magnetic entropy change ΔSM of about 2.0 J kg−1 K−1 under a 1 T field change (≈5 J kg−1 K−1 at 5 T), a refrigerant capacity RC of ≈55 J kg−1 (≈150 J kg−1 at 5 T), and a Curie temperature shifted to near 300 K (guess).

score.note: The recollection reverses the key substitution: Co replaced Ni, not Fe. It correctly identifies the predominant hexagonal Ni2In-type phase and slight lattice changes, although minor orthorhombic phase occurred only at x=0.40. The mechanism is only broadly plausible and omits austenite stabilization, lowered transition temperatures, and structural-magnetic coupling. Reported magnetocaloric values are far below the actual peaks (48.5 J kg−1 K−1 at 5 T for x=0.40), while only the approximate near-room-temperature transition is close.
